g.text: Database Indexing: B-Tree Lookup vs. Full Scan
Same table, 1,000,000 rows, one query: WHERE user_id = ?
Only the highlighted path (root -> internal -> leaf) is ever touched.
B-tree lookup touches ~3 levels: roughly 20 comparisons total.
Every row is compared -- there is no shortcut to skip any of them.
Full scan touches all 1,000,000 of them, every time.
Composite index (url_id, occurred_at): column order decides what it can serve
Narrows to one link's rows FIRST, then the date range within them.
Can't narrow by url_id first -- scans every link's rows in the date range.
